calls.summary: Marcus Delgado called about a knee replacement after years of arthritis pain. Rosey reviewed his imaging history, confirmed Denver Health accepts his plan, and scheduled a new-patient consultation with an adult reconstruction surgeon. Marcus was reassured and confirmed the visit before hanging up.

Angela Pruitt called to arrange physical therapy after her recent shoulder surgery. Lila located her surgeon's rehab order and booked a series of sessions at the orthopedics clinic. Angela was grateful and asked about parking, which Lila explained clearly.

David Okafor called to check on results from his knee MRI ordered last week. Oscar confirmed the images were read and that the surgeon's office would call with findings within 24-48h. David appreciated the clear timeline and stayed calm throughout.

Bethany Cruz, a new patient and recreational runner, called to set up a sports medicine evaluation for ongoing ankle pain. Mary collected her full contact details, insurance information, and injury history, then scheduled the intake consultation with a sports medicine provider. Bethany confirmed the date and requested a reminder text.

Frank Sullivan called wanting a cost estimate for a possible total knee replacement. Lee walked him through the consultation-first process and scheduled a new-patient orthopedic visit to evaluate his knee. Frank still had billing questions but agreed to come in.

Nadia Kensington called after a fall left her with a suspected wrist fracture. Sue advised urgent evaluation and booked a same-week fracture care consultation with the trauma team. Nadia was anxious but relieved to have an appointment secured.

Gregory Alvarado disputed a charge on his bill for a carpal tunnel release he had last month. Mike reviewed the itemized statement and opened a billing inquiry with financial services. Gregory remained frustrated but accepted the follow-up.

Priya Ramachandran complained that her physical therapy sessions kept getting rescheduled. Jennifer apologized, verified the clinic's availability, and locked in a consistent weekly time. Priya was still irritated by the earlier confusion.

Tyler Brennan, a high school coach's referral, called about a sports medicine assessment for a possible ACL tear. Rose gathered his information and scheduled a new evaluation, though the first available slot was further out than he hoped. He booked it anyway.

Denise Holloway called about a large bill following her knee MRI and asked why it was not fully covered. Oscar explained the imaging costs and referred her to financial assistance. Denise was upset about the amount and asked to escalate.

Samuel Ortega called about numbness in his hand and a possible carpal tunnel problem. Lila collected his details and scheduled a hand and upper extremity consultation despite a long hold earlier in the call. Samuel confirmed but noted the wait time was frustrating.

Carla Whitfield called because her cast from a recent fracture felt too tight and painful. Lee flagged it as urgent and arranged a same-day check, but Carla was distressed about being transferred twice. The issue was routed to the trauma clinic.

Raymond Fisk called to cancel his upcoming spine consultation because he found a closer provider. Jennifer processed the cancellation and offered to keep his records active. Raymond was curt and declined a reschedule.

Loretta Simmons called angry about being billed twice for a corticosteroid joint injection. Mike struggled to locate the duplicate charge and the call grew tense before he promised a callback. Loretta remained dissatisfied at the end.

Howard Mackenzie called after hours seeking to schedule a foot and ankle consultation and rolled to voicemail. He left a rushed message with only a partial callback number. No agent was available and the message was queued for the next business day.

prompts.question: Is the patient trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes, the caller has a right shoulder injury from a work accident approximately four weeks ago. She wants an evaluation for possible rotator cuff damage and is seeking surgical consultation if needed.

prompts.question: What are the patient's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects a timely consultation appointment with an orthopedic surgeon, wants imaging to be arranged during the visit, and hopes for a clear diagnosis and treatment plan for her shoulder.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have captured the caller's email address for appointment confirmation and should have briefly explained what to expect during the consultation visit, such as range-of-motion testing and possible X-ray ordering in clinic.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Denver Health Orthopedics. This is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. Yes, I injured my shoulder about a month ago at work. I need to see an orthopedic surgeon. I heard Denver Health has a great orthopedics team.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I am sorry to hear that. We definitely can help you. I would be happy to schedule a consultation with one of our orthopedic surgeons. Can I get your full name first, please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Of course. It is Sarah Mitchell.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Sarah. And just to make sure we get you to the right specialist, can you tell me a bit more about your shoulder injury? What happened?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I fell off a ladder at a construction site and landed hard on my right shoulder. Since then I have had pain and I cannot lift my arm very well. My primary care doctor said I should see an orthopedic surgeon to check for rotator cuff damage.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. That definitely sounds like something we need to evaluate. A rotator cuff evaluation is right in our wheelhouse. What ZIP code are you calling from, Sarah?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I live in Denver. My ZIP is 80202.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. We serve the Denver metro area and you are definitely in our service area. Now let me get your contact information. What is the best phone number to reach you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: You can reach me at ****-***-**** extension 4521.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, thank you. And I also want to make sure we have your email so we can send you appointment details and any forms you may need to complete beforehand.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Oh, actually I prefer not to give my email over the phone. Can you just call me to confirm everything?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. We will call you to confirm. Now let us get you scheduled. We have several appointments available next week. We have Tuesday morning at 10:00 AM or Wednesday afternoon at 2:00 PM. Which works better for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Tuesday morning works great for me. 10:00 AM is perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. So I have you down for Tuesday, October 29th at 10:00 AM with our orthopedic team at our central Denver clinic location. We will give you a call on Monday to confirm. Thank you for choosing Denver Health, Sarah. We look forward to seeing you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thank you, Marcus. I really appreciate it. Bye.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You are welcome. Take care.

callDetail.aiSummary: Sarah Mitchell, a new Denver Health orthopedic patient, called to schedule a consultation for a right shoulder injury sustained in a work accident approximately four weeks prior. She reported pain and limited range of motion consistent with possible rotator cuff damage, as recommended by her primary care physician. Marcus Bell successfully captured her name, contact phone number, and service area confirmation, and booked her for a Tuesday morning appointment at the central Denver clinic. However, her email address was not captured, and specific expectations for the consultation visit were not discussed.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great job on the overall structure and pacing of this call. You greeted professionally, qualified the chief complaint clearly, and confirmed service area before scheduling. The booking felt natural and the appointment detail was solid. Two coaching points. First, when Sarah declined to share her email, you could have acknowledged her preference and offered an alternative like sending a text message or having the confirmation call include the details verbally. Second, you could have briefly set expectations for the visit. For example, you might have said, 'When you come in on Tuesday, our surgeon will do a range-of-motion exam and may order imaging like an X-ray or MRI to get a complete picture of your rotator cuff. The whole visit usually takes about 30 to 45 minutes.' Small additions like that reduce patient anxiety and improve satisfaction. Otherwise, excellent work.

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as Denver Health's AI scheduling assistant helping the patient get personalized orthopedic care information and a preliminary cost range, mention that new-patient orthopedic consultations are currently booking quickly and financial assistance may be available, then ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one at a time: Ask only one question per message, covering which body area or injury is involved, how long symptoms have been present, whether they have had recent imaging such as X-ray or MRI, their insurance or coverage type including Medicaid, and finally their ZIP code to confirm they are within our service area.

Estimate then book: Confirm we serve their ZIP, share a general preliminary cost range for the likely service, explain that an exact quote requires an in-clinic evaluation with an orthopedic specialist, propose a specific day and time for the consultation, and let them know they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: Do I need a referral to see an orthopedic specialist at Denver Health?
qaPairs.answer: Many patients can self-refer for an orthopedic consultation, though some insurance plans require a referral. I can help you book a new-patient consultation and the team will confirm any referral needs.

qaPairs.question: Do you accept Medicaid?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Denver Health is a public health system that accepts Medicaid and works with many plans. I can get you scheduled for a consultation where our team will review your coverage.

qaPairs.question: How much does an orthopedic consultation cost?
qaPairs.answer: A new-patient consultation generally falls in a modest office-visit range, but your exact cost depends on your coverage and needs. The best step is to book a consultation so our team can give you an accurate estimate.

qaPairs.question: How much does a knee replacement cost?
qaPairs.answer: Total knee replacement costs vary widely based on your plan and care plan, so I cannot quote an exact figure by text. Let me schedule you with a joint replacement specialist who can give you a precise estimate.

qaPairs.question: I think I broke a bone, what should I do?
qaPairs.answer: If this is a severe or emergency injury please call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department right away. For non-emergency fracture care I can help you book an urgent orthopedic consultation quickly.

qaPairs.question: Can you treat a torn ACL?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our sports medicine and orthopedic surgeons evaluate and treat ACL injuries, including arthroscopic repair when needed. Let me set up a consultation so a specialist can assess your knee.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer physical therapy?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Denver Health provides physical therapy and rehabilitation for recovery, strengthening, and range of motion. I can help schedule an evaluation to start your therapy plan.

qaPairs.question: Where is the orthopedics clinic located?
qaPairs.answer: Our orthopedics services are offered at Denver Health locations in the Denver area. Tell me your ZIP code and I will confirm the most convenient clinic and book your visit.

qaPairs.question: Can I get help with the cost if I am uninsured?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, as a safety-net health system we offer financial assistance and sliding-scale options for eligible patients. I can book your consultation and connect you with a financial counselor.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat rotator cuff injuries?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our shoulder specialists diagnose and repair rotator cuff injuries, often with minimally invasive arthroscopy. Let me schedule a consultation so a specialist can review your shoulder.

qaPairs.question: How soon can I be seen?
qaPairs.answer: Availability varies by service and provider, but we work to get new patients in promptly. Share your ZIP and preferred time and I will find the soonest consultation slot.

qaPairs.question: Do you do carpal tunnel surgery?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our hand and upper extremity team performs carpal tunnel release as an outpatient procedure. I can book you a consultation to confirm whether it is right for you.

qaPairs.question: Can you help with chronic back pain?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our spine care team evaluates disc, stenosis, and degenerative conditions and builds a treatment plan. Let me schedule a spine consultation for you.

qaPairs.question: Do you see children for orthopedic issues?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer pediatric orthopedics for children's fractures, growth concerns, and injuries. I can book a consultation with our pediatric orthopedic team.

qaPairs.question: Do I need an MRI before my visit?
qaPairs.answer: Not necessarily, your specialist will decide what imaging is needed during your evaluation. Let me get you booked and they will order any imaging that is appropriate.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a corticosteroid injection for joint pain?
qaPairs.answer: Image-guided joint injections are one of the options our team offers for pain relief. Book a consultation and a specialist will determine if an injection is a good fit.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer sports injury evaluations for athletes?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our sports medicine team handles injury assessment and return-to-play planning. I can schedule a sports medicine evaluation for you.

qaPairs.question: What should I bring to my appointment?
qaPairs.answer: Bring your ID, insurance information, a list of medications, and any prior imaging or records if you have them. Let me confirm your consultation date so you can prepare.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat foot and ankle problems?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our foot and ankle specialists treat deformity, arthritis, and trauma with both non-surgical and surgical care. I can book a consultation to get you assessed.

qaPairs.question: Can I book an appointment right now?
qaPairs.answer: Absolutely, I can help you book an orthopedic consultation today. Just share your ZIP code and a preferred day and time to get started.
